page: Vultr vbm-6c-32gb-amd is a bare-metal server belonging to the Bare Metal NVMe family, powered by a single AMD EPYC 4245P processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the CPU provides 6 physical cores and 12 threads with dedicated allocation and a base clock speed of 3.8 GHz. The processor includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions, cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI, and AMD SVM virtualization. The server is configured with 32.0 GB of memory (2.67 GB per core) and bundles a dedicated 1920 GB NVMe SSD. Networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without hypervisor overhead.

Benchmark results highlight high-frequency execution in single-core workloads. In stress-ng single-core tests, the server recorded 4538.09, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, matched by a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 3380.0. Single-threaded data transformation demonstrated similar strength, reaching 49.16 GB/sec in gzip compression and 22.02 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Multi-core performance falls within median parameters, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 14983.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 31542.86. Lightweight language model inference on a 135M model achieved top-tier throughput at 430.19 tokens per second for text generation.

Hardware tradeoffs are visible in memory throughput and multi-threaded scaling. While small-block cached memory bandwidth reached 1624.4 GB/sec, large-block uncached memory write throughput registered 23.57 GB/sec, placing it in the lower 25 percent bracket. With 6 physical cores and a moderate 32 GB memory capacity, this bare-metal platform provides efficient compute-to-cost density for applications reliant on raw per-core clock speed and direct NVMe storage throughput rather than extreme core counts. Workload fits include continuous integration build nodes, single-threaded batch processing, edge web applications, and standalone relational databases.
description: Vultr vbm-6c-32gb-amd is a dedicated bare-metal server equipped with an AMD EPYC 4245P processor offering 6 physical cores and 12 threads at 3.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server incorporates 32 GB of system memory, a bundled 1920 GB NVMe SSD, and one complimentary public IPv4 address, operating completely without hypervisor abstraction. Performance benchmarks demonstrate top-tier single-thread throughput, including a Geekbench single-core rating of 3380.0 and stress-ng score of 4538.09, alongside top-decile gzip compression and bzip3 decompression metrics. Multi-threaded CPU execution and static web serving register in average performance bands, whereas large-block memory write throughput shows lower bandwidth at 23.57 GB/sec. Given its high CPU clock rate and direct-attached NVMe storage, this server configuration fits software compilation pipelines, dedicated relational database instances, text processing, and single-thread intensive backend applications.
